components.name: Split-Flap Display
components.description: Signature atom: fixed character cells with a mid-height seam; tones white, amber, red, unlit; SEV variant on red fill.
components.html: SEV1IDENTRULED
components.css: .ds-flaps { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; padding: 12px; background: #0B0B0D; } .ds-flap { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px; } .ds-cell { position: relative; width: 19px; height: 30px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: linear-gradient(#17181B 0 49%, #121315 51% 100%); border-radius: 2px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-cell::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 50% 0 auto; border-top: 1px solid #000; } .ds-cell span { font-family: 'Sofia Sans Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1; text-transform: uppercase; color: #F2F2F2; animation: ds-flap .3s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 2; } .ds-amber .ds-cell span { color: #FFB000; } .ds-red .ds-cell span { color: #FF5A6E; } .ds-sev { gap: 0; } .ds-sev .ds-cell { background: #B00020; } .ds-sev .ds-cell::after { border-color: rgba(0,0,0,.35); } .ds-lamp { width: 10px; height: 10px; margin-right: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 35%, #FFE6A6, #FFB000 55%, #A06E00); animation: ds-lamp 1.1s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-flap { 0% { transform: rotateX(0); filter: brightness(1); } 50% { transform: rotateX(-80deg); filter: brightness(.55); } 100% { transform: rotateX(0); filter: brightness(1); } } @keyframes ds-lamp { 50% { opacity: .35; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-cell span, .ds-lamp { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The investigation plays out on a concourse split-flap board. Suspect commits are departures, ranked by score; as the agent reads each diff, the row's status flaps over to IDENTIFIED under an amber lamp or to RULED OUT in red, struck through and left on the board. Everything sits on steel: dark frame panels set into a brushed-steel bezel, with flap-black boards inside them built from fixed character cells split by a hairline seam at mid-height. Information is read the way a traveller reads a board: condensed capitals, wide tracking, tabular figures, one row per thing.

The surface is an Operate tool, driven live by a presenter over a screen share at 1440x900 and read by an audience through compressed video. That sets the density and the contrast: large condensed caps, letter white on near-black, no meaning carried by colour alone (ruled-out rows are struck through as well as red; identified rows carry a lamp as well as amber). Replay is the default mode and every recording says it is a recording, in the mode switch, the run chip, the run note and the rail foot.

Motion has one grammar. Flaps flap; lamps pulse; the diff drawer opens and closes. Nothing else moves. The board refuses the category default of a dark dashboard of cards and charts, and the agent-as-chat-transcript.
keyCharacteristics: Split-flap cells are the system's atom: severity, the elapsed clock, commit hashes, statuses, the probable cause and confidence all render as flaps.
Steel frame, flap-black board, letter white: three material layers, no others.
Amber is the agent's colour and the board's lamp; red is cancellation.
Condensed caps for anything the board would print; plain sans for sentences a person reads; mono only for code.
Square corners everywhere except the 2px flap cell.
No shipping rasters: the brushed steel is inline SVG fractal noise over a gradient.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the agent and what it is doing (reading, identifying, reasoning, a match), the lamps, the primary action, and where focus or selection currently sits. It never decorates a heading, a border at rest, or a neutral control.

rules.name: The Never Removed Rule
rules.body: A ruled-out suspect stays on the board in red with its change text struck through. Red plus strike-through, never red alone, and never a disappearing row.

rules.name: The Board Prints Caps Rule
rules.body: If the board would print it (a title, status, hash, field name, column head, button), it is Sofia Sans Condensed uppercase with tracking. If a person or the agent wrote it as a sentence, it is Sofia Sans in sentence case.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Code Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only where the content is code: diffs, the git revert line, inline identifiers. Never for numbers or labels; numbers get tabular figures in the sans faces.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: Only panels and the primary action cast a shadow, and only a short soft one. Nothing floats, glows or blurs.

dos: Do render any status, hash, clock or verdict value that changes as a split-flap display, and let it cascade per cell (2-3 intermediate characters, 75ms ticks, 22ms stagger).
Do set every flap instantly and stop lamp pulses under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do keep a ruled-out row on the board in cancel-red-text with a 2px strike-through.
Do pair every colour signal with a second channel: strike-through, lamp, label or text.
Do label every replay as a recording, with its date and model, in the run chip, run note and rail foot; mark stand-ins as stand-ins.
Do keep amber for the agent, lamps, the primary action, and focus or current selection.
Do draw textures as inline SVG; the brushed steel is feTurbulence noise in a data URI.
Do size type for a compressed 1440x900 screen share: labels and metadata at 12-13px in caps or steel light, prose at 15-16px.
donts: Don't build the board out of rounded cards, charts or a chat transcript of the agent.
Don't remove a ruled-out suspect, or mark it with red alone.
Don't use amber for decoration, resting borders or headings.
Don't animate anything other than flaps, lamps and the diff drawer (short background-colour easing on hover and row state aside): no fades, slides or parallax.
Don't use JetBrains Mono outside code.
Don't ship raster textures or images in the demo.
